baselineFacts: Current AC97 write_audio stages up to4096 bytes and honors the accepted byte count from AUD_write; it is already a block path.
APU monitor opens SDL_OpenAudioDeviceStream for48000Hz S16LE stereo, queues frame buffers and destroys the stream at finalize.
Current ACI owns its AC97LinkState but has no shared APU output seam.
Replacement must preserve partial accepted writes, guest DMA advancement, volume/mute, BUP, independent AC97 playback, callback lifetime and queue latency.
AUD_write already has a non-mixing backend path selected by mixing_engine=false. That is a useful diagnostic baseline, not proof of shared output or preserved volume/rate semantics.

Without a backend volume_out callback, codec gain/mute is applied in audio_pcm_sw_write. The non-mixing AUD_write branch bypasses that software path, so it cannot be proposed as a universal gain-preserving switch.
Current audio/meson.build comments out the SDL QEMU backend, although the APU uses SDL3 directly. The old SDL2 sdlaudio.c is not the live AC97 backend just because it remains in the tree.
APU output is submitted after every eighth EP frame. Its throttle reads this stream queue and pauses/backoffs under the APU mutex, independently of AC97 guest DMA.
APU off/halt/trap takes a timed wait and skips se_frame; a shared AC97 consumer placed only in se_frame would stop servicing independent AC97 playback.

query-audiodevs iterates explicit audiodevs; implicit #default is created through a separate default list and registered under /audiodevs. An empty query result alone cannot identify or rule out a selected default backend.
The retained PGR2 launch has no explicit -audiodev argument. Retained stdout/stderr have no backend identification. No current AC97-heavy cost is established.

officialSources.lesson: Convenience stream owns device lifetime; destroying it closes the associated device.
Multiple logical devices may share one physical device; opening twice is not proof of two hardware devices.
SDL can mix multiple bound streams; already-bound streams need explicit unbinding.

remaining: Resolve inferred AC97 none-backend fallback in the exact native release build before proposing a shared audible-output performance comparison; adding audible output is a functionality change, not an equivalent-work speedup.
Profile actual AC97-heavy playback and establish its host-output cost before a candidate.
Identify current QEMU host backend and actual physical/logical SDL devices; separate dispatch/mixing from output cost.
Recheck main/upstream and closed/open PR work at implementation time.
Compare SDL-managed shared-device ownership before inventing a ring transport.
Compare existing QEMU non-mixing output when supported, retaining codec gain, format/rate and queue/progress semantics; do not treat disabling behavior as performance.
Capture default /audiodevs ownership as well as explicit device queries on the next diagnostic run; bind backend identity to real AC97 activity before comparing output cost.
